correctness.rationale: The four prime-power rows and the integral finding hold. Independent exact norm/elimination recovers the 22-degree affine polynomial, absolute discriminant 2^42*7^77, the linear subresultant D y+N, and the unit denominator resultants at every factor (including x). Substitution of -N/D satisfies both equations modulo the eliminant. The norm belongs to the affine ideal by the multiplication-matrix adjugate; the linear subresultant then makes the affine Hessian intersection over Z[1/42] exactly the graph over its projection. At the two infinity vertices the local linear parts of the curve and sextic are the two chart parameters in opposite roles, so the sections are étale and separate components of the finite intersection. The fiberwise 24 simple intersections are ordinary, since tangent contacts 3 and 4 give Hessian orders 1 and 2 in the allowed characteristics. Orbit products of the stated cyclotomic generators give degrees 3,6,6,6, with discriminants 7^2,-7^5,-2^6*7^5,-2^6*7^5, so the order indices are units on the base. This proves the relative decomposition and makes q-Frobenius the stated regular actions and quotient action. The standard monic-f resultant is +x times the four factors, not minus as printed; at x=1 the Sylvester determinant is -232 and SymPy 1.14.0 gives +232. Only the unit-normalized eliminant matters. Reproduction: python /workspace/flex_and_octic_reproduction.py (SymPy 1.14.0); frozen VERIFY.py only inspected.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: There is a canonical map from the three constant sections, the real cyclotomic orbit, and the three full cyclotomic orbits to the relative flex intersection. The correct discriminants make the source finite étale over Z[1/42]; in every geometric fiber this is an isomorphism by separation and Bézout. The target is finite étale by properness, finite fibers and the relative Jacobian criterion (transversality). Thus the map is an isomorphism. This mechanically gives the claimed decomposition from the sibling, without a new arithmetic theorem. The classical symmetry passages inspected are related but do not themselves print the four arithmetic rows.
